claim: Hydroxyethyl starch (HES) is a safe and effective fluid for volume resuscitation in critically ill adults

rows.finding: Joachim Boldt RCT: 6% HES 130/0.42 vs albumin priming for cardiopulmonary bypass in 50 CABG patients; falsely reported HES REDUCED inflammation (IL-6/IL-10), endothelial damage (ICAM-1), renal tubular injury (a-GST, NGAL) and better preserved coagulation/platelet function - i.e. made HES look protective and safe. FABRICATED: retracted by Anesthesia & Analgesia (Dec 2010, PMID:21106980); the 2014 editor's note (PMID:25329035) names this exact paper and states the Klinikum Ludwigshafen investigation 'determined that the study was fabricated' (no IRB approval, no informed consent, missing/fabricated data). Cardiac-surgery CPB-priming population, not general critically-ill ICU resuscitation.
rows.citation: Boldt J, et al. Cardiopulmonary bypass priming using a high dose of a balanced hydroxyethyl starch versus an albumin-based priming strategy. Anesth Analg. 2009;109(6):1752-62. RETRACTED. DOI 10.1213/ANE.0b013e3181b5a24b
rows.integrity_note: RETRACTED / FABRICATED. PubMed article-type flag: 'Retracted Publication'. Retraction notice: Shafer SL. Notice of retraction. Anesth Analg. 2010;111(6):1567 (PMID:21106980, DOI 10.1213/ANE.0b013e3182040b99). Reaffirmed by editor's note PMID:25329035 (2014) which names this HES-vs-albumin CPB-priming paper and states the Klinikum Ludwigshafen investigation found it fabricated. Part of the ~88/89-article joint retraction (18 editors-in-chief, 2011); Boldt is anesthesiology's retraction record-holder (>180 papers). His fabricated trials systematically made HES appear safe/effective; excluding them flips the honest verdict to harm (Not Supported).

rows.finding: VISEP trial. In 537 evaluable patients with severe sepsis, 10% pentastarch (HES 200/0.5) vs modified Ringer's lactate. HES caused higher rates of acute renal failure and renal-replacement therapy, with toxicity increasing with cumulative dose; trial stopped early for safety. Authors: 'As used in this study, HES was harmful, and its toxicity increased with accumulating doses.' (NCT00135473)
rows.citation: Brunkhorst FM, et al. Intensive insulin therapy and pentastarch resuscitation in severe sepsis. N Engl J Med. 2008;358(2):125-39. NCT00135473. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa070716

rows.finding: 6S trial. 804 patients with severe sepsis randomized to 6% HES 130/0.42 (Tetraspan) vs Ringer's acetate. At 90 days, death 51% (HES) vs 43% (Ringer's), relative risk 1.17 (95% CI 1.01-1.36, P=0.03); more renal-replacement therapy (22% vs 16%, RR 1.35, 95% CI 1.01-1.80, P=0.04) and a trend to more severe bleeding (10% vs 6%). HES increased death and RRT.
rows.citation: Perner A, et al. Hydroxyethyl starch 130/0.42 versus Ringer's acetate in severe sepsis. N Engl J Med. 2012;367(2):124-34. NCT00962156. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1204242

rows.finding: CHEST trial. 7000 ICU patients randomized to 6% HES 130/0.4 (Voluven) vs 0.9% saline. No mortality benefit (90-day death 18.0% vs 17.0%, RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96-1.18, NS) but MORE renal-replacement therapy (7.0% vs 5.8%, RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.00-1.45, P=0.04) and significantly more adverse events (5.3% vs 2.8%, P<0.001). HES gave no benefit and more renal harm in general critically ill adults.
rows.citation: Myburgh JA, et al. Hydroxyethyl starch or saline for fluid resuscitation in intensive care (CHEST). N Engl J Med. 2012;367(20):1901-11. NCT00935168. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1209759

rows.finding: Systematic review + meta-analysis + trial sequential analysis of 9 RCTs (3456 sepsis patients) of HES 130/0.38-0.45 vs crystalloid or albumin. HES increased renal-replacement therapy (RR 1.36, 1.08-1.72), red-cell transfusion (RR 1.29, 1.13-1.48) and serious adverse events (RR 1.30, 1.02-1.67); in low-risk-of-bias trials the relative risk of death was 1.11 (1.00-1.23). Authors: 'unlikely that HES 130/0.38-0.45 provides overall clinical benefit for patients with sepsis.' Clean, post-Boldt evidence synthesis.
rows.citation: Haase N, Perner A, et al. Hydroxyethyl starch 130/0.38-0.45 versus crystalloid or albumin in patients with sepsis: systematic review with meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis. BMJ. 2013;346:f839. DOI 10.1136/bmj.f839

rows.finding: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 trials (4624 septic patients), HES vs crystalloid. HES increased acute kidney injury (RR 1.24, 1.13-1.36), need for renal-replacement therapy (RR 1.36, 1.17-1.57), red-cell transfusion (RR 1.14, 1.01-1.93) and 90-day mortality (RR 1.14, 1.04-1.26). Authors favor crystalloids over HES for sepsis resuscitation.
rows.citation: Serpa Neto A, et al. Fluid resuscitation with hydroxyethyl starches in patients with sepsis is associated with an increased incidence of acute kidney injury and use of renal replacement therapy: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Crit Care. 2013;29(1):185.e1-7. DOI 10.1016/j.jcrc.2013.09.031

integrity_records.study: Boldt J, et al. Cardiopulmonary bypass priming using a high dose of a balanced hydroxyethyl starch versus an albumin-based priming strategy. Anesth Analg. 2009;109(6):1752-62 (PMID:19923501, DOI 10.1213/ANE.0b013e3181b5a24b)
integrity_records.wording: RETRACTED and flagged 'Retracted Publication' on PubMed. Formal retraction notice: Shafer SL, Notice of retraction, Anesth Analg 2010;111(6):1567 (PMID:21106980, DOI 10.1213/ANE.0b013e3182040b99); the study was retracted December 2010 for lack of IRB approval. The 2014 editor's note (Shafer SL, Anesth Analg 2014;119(5):1225, PMID:25329035, DOI 10.1213/ANE.0000000000000417) names this exact HES-vs-albumin CPB-priming paper and states the Klinikum Ludwigshafen investigation 'determined that the study was fabricated' (no IRB approval, no written informed consent, missing/fabricated patient and laboratory data; albumin priming described though the hospital had not stocked albumin for cardiac surgery since 1999). Part of the joint retraction of ~88 Boldt articles by 18 editors-in-chief (2011); Boldt is anesthesiology's retraction record-holder (>180 papers). His fabricated trials systematically made HES appear safe and effective; excluding them flips the honest verdict to harm (Not Supported).

integrity_records.study: Joachim Boldt fraud investigation (institutional) — Landesaerztekammer Rheinland-Pfalz / Klinikum Ludwigshafen; joint editors-in-chief retraction statement (2011)
integrity_records.wording: Landesaerztekammer Rheinland-Pfalz (State Medical Board) reported no IRB approval for 89 Boldt articles (1999-2011); Anesthesia & Analgesia retracted 22 of its Boldt papers in 2011 for unethical conduct of research. Klinikum Ludwigshafen's investigation found the studies 'failed to meet required standards,' included 'false data' in at least 10 studies, and found 'clear evidence of procedural irregularities and research misconduct.' Documented by Retraction Watch and by Anesthesia & Analgesia's own retraction announcement.
